translations.text: Second Vision
In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of the Babylonians came to Jerusalem and besieged it.

The Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hands, along with some of the vessels of the house of God. He took them to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, and brought the vessels into his god’s treasury.
The king told Ashpenaz, his chief eunuch, to bring some of the captive Israelites, some of the royal offspring, and some of the Parthians:

young men without blemish, handsome in appearance, discerning in all wisdom, knowledgeable, trained in understanding, and capable of serving in the palace before the king, and to teach them the literature and language of the Chaldeans.
The king assigned them a daily allowance from the king’s table and from the wine he himself drank. They were to be nourished for three years and then placed in service before the king.
Among them were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, from the people of Judah.
And the chief eunuch gave them names: to Daniel, Belteshazzar; to Hananiah, Shadrach; to Mishael, Meshach; and to Azariah, Abednego.
Daniel resolved in his heart not to eat from the king’s table or drink his wine, and he begged the chief eunuch that he might not eat it.
God granted Daniel favor and compassion in the sight of the chief eunuch.

The chief eunuch said to Daniel, “I fear my lord the king, who has assigned your food and drink. He might see your faces looking more downcast than those of the other young men your age, and you would make me liable to death before the king.”
And Daniel said to Amelsad, whom the chief eunuch had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
“Please test your servants for ten days. Let us be given pulses to eat and water to drink,
and let our complexions and the complexions of the young men who eat from the king’s table be examined before you. Then deal with your servants according to what you see.”
And he listened to them and tested them for ten days.
At the end of the ten days, their faces appeared healthier to him, and they were stronger in body than all the young men who ate from the king’s table.
Amelgasad would take away their meals and the wine they were to drink and give pulses to the four young men.
And God gave them wisdom and understanding in all learning and wisdom, and Daniel understood every vision and dream.
At the end of the appointed days, the king commanded that they be brought in, and the chief eunuch brought them before Nebuchadnezzar.
The king spoke with them, and among them all none were found like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. They served before the king.
In every matter of wisdom and knowledge about which the king questioned them, he found them ten times better than all the diviners and magicians in his kingdom.
Daniel remained until the years of King Cyrus.
Third Vision
In the second year of his reign, Nebuchadnezzar had a dream. His spirit was bewildered, and sleep left him.
The king said, “Summon the diviners, magicians, sorcerers, and Chaldeans to tell the king his dream.” They came and stood before the king.
The king said to them, “I have had a dream, and my spirit is bewildered as I seek to understand the dream.”
The Chaldeans spoke to the king in Aramaic: “O king, live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will give its interpretation.”
The king answered the Chaldeans, “The matter has gone from me. Now, if you do not reveal the dream and its interpretation to me, you will be destroyed, and your houses will be plundered.
But if you reveal the dream and its interpretation to me, you will receive rewards, many gifts, and honors from me. Just tell me the dream and its interpretation.”
They answered a second time, saying, “Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will explain its interpretation.”
The king answered, “I know for certain that you are buying time, because you see that the matter has gone from me.

So if you do not tell me the dream, I know that you have agreed to speak lying and deceptive words before me until the time passes. Tell me my dream, and I will know that you will also tell me its interpretation.”
The Chaldeans answered the king again, saying, “There is no one on earth who can reveal the king’s matter, for no great king or ruler asks such a thing of a learned man, a magician, or a Chaldean.
The thing the king asks is difficult, and no one can tell it to the king except the gods, who do not dwell among mortal beings.”
Then the king, in great anger and fury, ordered all the wise men of Babylon to be killed.
The order went out, and the wise men were being killed. They also sought Daniel and his companions to put them to death.
Then Daniel spoke with wisdom and discretion to Arioch, the king’s chief executioner, an officer of the king who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.
He asked him, “Why has this harsh order come from the king?” And Arioch explained the matter to Daniel.
Daniel went in and begged the king to give him time, so that he could tell the king the interpretation.
Daniel went to his house and told his companions Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael about the matter.
They sought mercy from the God of heaven, so that Daniel and his companions would not perish with the other wise men of Babylon.
Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision during the night, and Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
And he said, “May the name of the Lord be blessed from eternity to eternity, for wisdom, understanding, and power belong to him.”
And he changes the times and seasons; he establishes kings and replaces them. He gives wisdom to the wise and understanding to those with discernment.
He reveals deep and hidden things; he knows what is in the darkness, and light is with him.
I thank and bless you, God of our fathers, because you have given me wisdom and strength. You have made known to me what we asked of you in prayer, and you have shown me the king’s vision.

Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon, and said to him, “Do not kill the wise men of Babylon. Instead, take me before the king, and I will tell the king the interpretation.”
Then Arioch hurriedly brought Daniel before the king and said to him, “I have found a man among the captives from Judah who will tell the king the interpretation.”
The king addressed Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, saying, “Can you tell me the dream I saw and its interpretation?”
Daniel answered the king, saying, “The mystery the king asks about cannot be told to the king by wise men, magicians, learned men, or diviners.
But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, and he has shown King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the last days. Your dream and the vision in your mind as you lay on your bed are these:
O king, your thoughts troubled you on your bed about what would happen after this, and the revealer of mysteries showed you what would happen.

This mystery was revealed to me not because I have more wisdom than any other living person, but so that the interpretation might be made known to the king, and so that you might know the thoughts of your heart.
You, O king, were looking, and there was a statue, a great statue. Its face and its appearance were exceedingly dreadful, and it stood before you. The statue was exceedingly terrifying.
Its head was of pure gold; its hands, chest, and arms were of silver; its waist and thighs were of bronze;
and its legs were of iron, and its feet were partly of iron and partly of earthenware.
You watched until a stone was cut out without hands, and it struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and crushed them completely.

Then the clay, iron, bronze, silver, and gold were all crushed together and became like dust on a summer threshing floor. The force of the wind carried them away, and no place was found for them. But the stone that struck the image became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
This is the dream, and we will tell its interpretation before the king.
You, O king, are king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given a mighty and glorious kingdom.
Wherever human beings dwell, he has given the beasts of the field, the birds of heaven, and the fish of the sea into your hands and has made you lord of them all. You are the head of gold.
After you another kingdom will arise, inferior to yours, and a third kingdom, which is the bronze, will rule over the whole earth.
The fourth kingdom will be strong as iron. Just as iron crushes and grinds everything, so it will crush and grind everything.
As you saw the feet and toes partly of iron and partly of clay, the kingdom will be divided, but it will have some of the firmness of iron, just as you saw the iron mixed with clay.
And the toes of the feet were partly iron and partly clay: one part of the kingdom will be strong, and part of it will be brittle.
As you saw the iron mixed with clay, they will mix through human offspring, but they will not cling to one another, just as iron does not mix with clay.

In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will establish a kingdom that will never be destroyed. His kingdom will not be left to another nation. It will crush and sweep away all the kingdoms, but it will itself stand forever.

Just as you saw that the stone was cut from the mountain without hands and crushed the clay, iron, bronze, silver, and gold, the great God has shown the king what will happen hereafter. The dream is true, and its interpretation is trustworthy.
Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face and bowed down to Daniel, and he commanded that sacrifices and fragrant incense be offered to him.
The king answered and said to Daniel, “Truly, your God is the God of gods, the Lord of lords, and the King of kings, who reveals mysteries, since you were able to reveal this mystery.”
The king exalted Daniel and gave him many great gifts. He appointed him over the province of Babylon and made him chief ruler over all the wise men of Babylon.
Daniel made a request of the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over the affairs of the province of Babylon. But Daniel remained at the king’s court.
Fourth Vision
In the eighteenth year of his reign, King Nebuchadnezzar made a golden image, sixty cubits high and six cubits wide, and set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.

He sent orders to assemble the satraps, generals, commanders, chiefs, rulers, administrators, and all the governors of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

Then the satraps, generals, commanders, chiefs, rulers, nobles, administrators, and all the governors of the provinces assembled to come to the dedication of the image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up. They stood before the image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
A herald proclaimed loudly, saying, “To you it is commanded, peoples, nations, and languages:
When you hear the sound of the trumpet, pipe, drum, lyre, harp, the harmony of songs, and every kind of musical instrument, fall down and worship the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar set up.
Whoever does not fall down and worship will at that very hour be thrown into the blazing fiery furnace.”

And when the peoples heard the sound of the trumpet, flute, harp, musical instruments, and instruments of every kind, all the peoples, nations, and speakers of every language fell down and worshiped the golden image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
Then some Chaldean men came forward and accused the Jews before Nebuchadnezzar.
They said, “O king, live forever!
You issued a command to everyone who hears the sound of the trumpet, flute, lyre, harp, musical instruments, and instruments of every kind.
Whoever does not fall down and worship the golden image shall be thrown into the blazing furnace.

Now there are Jewish men here whom you appointed over the affairs of the province of Babylon: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. They have not obeyed your command, O king. They do not serve your gods or worship the golden image that you set up.”
Then Nebuchadnezzar, in rage and anger, ordered Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to be brought, and they were brought before the king.
Nebuchadnezzar answered and said to them, “Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that you do not serve my gods or worship the golden image that I set up?

Now, if you are ready, when you hear the sound of the trumpet, flute, drum, lyre, and the harmony of instruments of every kind, fall down and worship the image that I made. But if you do not worship it, at that very hour you will be thrown into the blazing furnace. And who is the God who will rescue you from my hands?”
Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered King Nebuchadnezzar and said, “We have no need to give you an answer about this matter.
For our God, whom we serve, is in heaven. He is able to rescue us from this blazing furnace and to deliver us from your hands, O king.
But if not, let this be known to you, O king: we will not serve your gods or worship the golden image that you set up.”
Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with rage, and his expression changed toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He said, “Heat the furnace sevenfold, so that they may be burned completely.
And let five men of great strength bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to throw them into the blazing furnace.”
Then those men were bound in their robes, trousers, turbans, and leggings, and were thrown into the blazing furnace.
For the king’s command was severe, and the furnace blazed exceedingly fiercely, sevenfold hotter.
And those three, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell bound into the furnace.
They walked in the midst of the fire, blessing and praising the Lord God.
Azariah rose and stood in prayer. He opened his mouth in the midst of the fire and said:
“Blessed are you, Lord, God of our fathers. Your name is praised and glorified forever.
For you are just in everything you have brought upon us. All your works are true, your ways are upright, and all your judgments are true.
You have passed just judgments in everything you have done to us and to Jerusalem, the holy city of our fathers.
For in truth and justice you have brought all this upon us because of our sins. We have sinned and acted lawlessly by rebelling against you, and we have sinned greatly in everything.
We have not obeyed your commandments, kept them, or done as you commanded us so that it might go well with us.
Everything you have brought upon us and everything you have done to us, you have done with just judgment.
And you handed us over to our enemies, who are lawless, cruel, and rebellious, and to a king more unjust and evil than any on earth.
And now we cannot open our mouths, for we have become a shame and a disgrace to your servants who minister to you.
But do not abandon us completely, for your name’s sake; do not break your covenant, and do not take your mercy away from us.
For the sake of Abraham, whom you love, and for the sake of Isaac your servant and Israel your holy one.
To whom you promised to multiply their offspring like the stars of heaven and like the sand on the seashore.
And now, Lord, we have become fewer than any other nation, and today we are afflicted throughout the earth because of our sins.
At this time there is no ruler, prophet, or leader, no burnt offerings, sacrifices, offerings, or incense, and no place to offer firstfruits before you and find mercy.
But may we be accepted with broken hearts and afflicted spirits,

as though with burnt offerings of rams and bulls and with tens of thousands of fattened lambs. So may our offering be before you today, that we may follow you fully, for those who hope in you are not put to shame.
And now we follow you with all our hearts, and we fear you and seek your face.
Do not put us to shame, but deal with us according to your gentleness and your abundant mercy.
And deliver us through your wondrous deeds, and give glory to your name, Lord.
And let all who do evil to your servants be put to shame; let them be ashamed of all their violence, and let their power be shattered.
And let them know that you alone are the Lord God, glorified over the whole world.
And the king’s servants who had thrown them in did not stop stoking the furnace with naphtha, oil, flax, and vine wood.
And the flame rose and towered forty-nine cubits above the furnace.
And it moved about, surrounding the furnace, and burned those of the Chaldeans whom it found.
And the angel of God came down and stood with Azariah and his companions there in the furnace, and drove the fiery flame out of the furnace.
And he made the inside of the furnace like a wind blowing with dew, and the fire did not come near them at all, nor did it distress or trouble them.
Then the three, as though with one mouth, blessed and praised and glorified God in the furnace, saying:
Blessed are you, Lord God of our ancestors, praised and exalted above all forever; and blessed is your holy and glorious name, praised and exalted above all forever.
Blessed are you in the temple of your holy glory, praised and exalted above all forever.
Blessed are you on the throne of your kingdom, praised and exalted above all forever.
Blessed are you who look into the depths and sit upon the cherubim, praised and exalted above all forever.
Blessed are you who sit in the firmament of heaven, praised and exalted above all forever.
All works of the Lord, bless the Lord; bless him and exalt him forever.
Heavens, bless the Lord; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, angels of the Lord; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all waters above the heavens; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all powers of the Lord; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, sun and moon; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all stars of heaven; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all rain and dew; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all winds; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, fire and heat; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, cold and ice; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, hoarfrost and snow; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, days and nights; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, light and darkness; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, clouds and lightning; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, earth; let it bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, mountains and hills; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all plants of the earth; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, springs; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, sea and rivers; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, whales and all creatures that frolic in the waters; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, birds of heaven; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, all wild beasts and livestock; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, children of humankind; bless him and exalt him forever.
Let Israel bless the Lord; let it bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, priests; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, servants of the Lord; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, spirits and souls of the righteous; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, you who are holy and humble in heart; bless him and exalt him forever.
Bless the Lord, Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael; bless him and exalt him forever.
For he rescued us from Hades and saved us from the hands of death.
And he saved us from this furnace and from the midst of this blazing flame, and from the midst of this fire he saved us.
Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
Bless the God of gods, all you servants of the Lord; bless him and give thanks, for his mercy endures forever.

When Nebuchadnezzar heard their praises, he was astonished. He rose in alarm and said to his nobles, “Did we not throw three men, bound, into the fire?” They said to the king, “Yes, you speak correctly, O king.”
The king said, “But I see four men, unbound, walking in the midst of the fire, and there is no harm in them. The appearance of the fourth is like a son of God.”

Then Nebuchadnezzar approached the opening of the blazing fiery furnace and said, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out and come here!” And Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out from the midst of the fire.

The nobles, governors, military commanders, and the king’s powerful men gathered and looked at the men: the fire had had no power over their bodies, the hair of their heads had not been singed, their trousers had not changed color, and there was no smell of fire on them.

The king bowed down before their Lord. Nebuchadnezzar then spoke and said, “Blessed is the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who sent his angel and saved his servants, because they trusted in him. They disregarded the king’s command and surrendered their bodies to the fire rather than serve or bow down to any gods except their own God alone.”

“And now I issue a decree: any nations, peoples, or languages that speak blasphemy against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego shall be handed over to destruction, and their houses to plunder, for there is no other god who can save in this way.”
Then the king gave Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego still greater honor in the land of the Babylonians and exalted them, and asked them to be rulers over all the Jews who were in his kingdom.
King Nebuchadnezzar, to all nations and languages dwelling throughout the earth: May peace increase for you.
It seemed good to me to tell you about the signs and wonders that the Most High performed for me,
how great and mighty they are! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and his dominion lasts from generation to generation.
The Fifth Vision
I, Nebuchadnezzar, was happy in my house and at ease.
I saw a dream, and it terrified me. I was troubled on my bed, and the vision in my head alarmed me.
I issued a command to bring before me all the wise men of the Babylonians, so that they might show me the interpretation of the dream.
The wise men, magi, [?], and Chaldeans came before me. I told them the dream, but they did not show me its interpretation.
At last Daniel came, whose name was Belteshazzar after the name of my god, because the Holy Spirit of God was in him.

I said to him, “Belteshazzar, ruler, know what I saw. I know that the Holy Spirit of God is in you, and no mysteries are hidden from you. Now listen to the vision of the dream that I saw, and tell me its interpretation.”
I was looking while on my bed, and behold, there was a tree in the midst of the earth, and its height was very great.
The tree grew great and strong, and its height reached to heaven, and its spread reached the ends of the whole earth.
Its leaves were beautiful and its fruit abundant, and in it there was food for all. The wild beasts lived beneath it, and the birds of heaven rested in its branches, and all flesh was fed from it.
I was watching in a vision of the night while on my bed, and behold, a watcher, a holy one, was coming down from heaven.
He cried out forcefully and said: “Cut down this tree and lop off its branches; shake off its leaves and scatter its fruit. Let the beasts move away from beneath it and the birds from its branches.

But leave its root stump in the earth, bound with iron and bronze, among the green growth of the field. Let it be drenched with the dew of heaven, and let its portion be with the beasts of the wilderness and in the grass of the earth.
Let his heart be changed from a human heart, and let a beast’s heart be given to him, and let seven periods of time pass over him.

This pronouncement is by the decision of the watcher, and this demand is the command of the holy ones, so that the living may know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humankind and gives it to whomever he wishes, and sets over it one despised among men.”

“This is the dream that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw. And you, Belteshazzar, tell me its interpretation, because none of the wise men of my kingdom could show me its interpretation. But you, Daniel, are able, because the Holy Spirit of God is in you.”

Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was stunned for about an hour, and his thoughts troubled him. The king spoke and said to him, “Belteshazzar, do not let the dream and its interpretation distress you.” Belteshazzar answered and said, “My lord, may the dream be for those who hate you, and its interpretation for your enemies!
The tree that you saw, grown great and strong, whose height reached to heaven and whose spread extended throughout the whole earth,
whose leaves were beautiful and whose fruit was abundant, and in which there was food for all, beneath which the beasts of the wilderness lived and in whose branches the birds of heaven rested—
it is you, O king, for you have grown great and strong. Your greatness has risen and reached to heaven, and your dominion to the ends of the whole earth.

And because you saw, O king, a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven and saying, ‘Cut down this tree and destroy it, but leave its root stump in the earth, bound with iron and bronze, among the green growth of the field. Let it be drenched with the dew of heaven, and let its portion be with the beasts of the wilderness until seven periods of time pass over it’—
this is its interpretation, O king, and it is the judgment of the Most High that has come upon my lord the king:

They will drive you away from humankind, and your dwelling will be with the beasts of the wilderness. They will feed you grass like an ox, and you will be drenched with the dew of heaven. Seven periods of time will pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humankind and gives it to whomever he wishes.
And because he said, ‘Leave the tree’s root stump,’ your kingdom will remain yours until you acknowledge the authority of the heavenly one.

Therefore, O king, let my counsel be acceptable to you: atone for your sins through almsgiving and for your lawless deeds through compassion for the poor. Perhaps God will be patient toward your transgressions.”
All this came upon King Nebuchadnezzar.
After twelve months, while he was walking on the roof of his royal palace in Babylon.
The king began to speak and said, “Is this not the great Babylon that I myself built as a royal residence by the might of my power and for the honor of my glory?”
While the words were still in the king’s mouth, a voice came from heaven and said, “To you I say, King Nebuchadnezzar: your kingdom has passed from you.

They will drive you away from human beings, and your dwelling will be with the wild beasts of the wilderness. They will feed you grass like an ox, and seven periods of time will pass over you, until you recognize that the Most High rules over the kingdom of human beings and gives it to whomever he wishes.”

At that very hour the word was fulfilled concerning Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven away from human beings and ate grass like an ox. His body was soaked with the dew of heaven, until his hair grew like lions’ hair and his nails like those of birds.

At the end of those days, I, Nebuchadnezzar, raised my eyes to heaven, and my understanding returned to me. I blessed the Most High and praised and glorified the one who lives forever, for his dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his rule endures from generation to generation.

All the inhabitants of the earth are counted as nothing. He acts according to his will among the host of heaven and the inhabitants of the earth. There is no one who can resist his hand and say, “What have you done?”

At that time my understanding returned to me, and I regained the honor of my kingdom, and my appearance was restored to me. My officials and my nobles sought me out, and I was established in my kingdom again, and still greater majesty was given to me.
Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, bless, exalt, and glorify the King of heaven, for all his works are true and his ways are just, and he is able to humble all who walk in pride.
King Belshazzar prepared a feast for a thousand of his nobles, and wine likewise for the thousand.

When Belshazzar came under the influence of wine, he ordered the silver and gold vessels brought which his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem, so that the king, his nobles, his concubines, and his wives might drink from them.
They brought the gold and silver vessels that had been taken from the temple of God in Jerusalem, and the king, his nobles, his concubines, and his wives drank from them.
They drank wine and praised the gods of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, but they did not praise the eternal God, who had authority over their souls.
At that very hour, the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote opposite the lampstand on the plaster of the wall of the king’s palace, and the king saw the hand that was writing.
Then the king’s color drained away, and his thoughts troubled him. The joints of his hips loosened, and his knees knocked against one another.

The king cried out loudly for the magicians, the Chaldeans, and the wise men to be brought in. He said to the wise men of Babylon, “Whoever reads this writing and shows me its interpretation will be clothed in purple, with a gold necklace around his neck, and will rule as third in my kingdom.”
All the king’s wise men came in, but they could not read the writing or show the king its interpretation.
King Belshazzar was troubled, and the color of his face changed. His nobles were troubled along with him.
The queen entered the banqueting hall and said, “O king, live forever! Do not let your thoughts trouble you, and do not let the color of your face change.

For there is a man in your kingdom in whom is the Holy Spirit of God. In the days of your father, powers and wisdom were found in him, and King Nebuchadnezzar, your father, appointed him chief over the wise men, magicians, Chaldeans, and diviners.

For Daniel has an exceptional spirit, wisdom, and understanding. He interprets dreams, explains riddles, and resolves tangled matters. The king gave him the name Belteshazzar. Now let him be summoned, and he will explain its interpretation.”
Then Daniel was brought in before the king, and the king said to Daniel, “Are you Daniel, one of the captives from Judea whom my father Nebuchadnezzar brought here?
I have heard about you that the Spirit of God is in you, and that strength, understanding, and exceptional wisdom have been found in you.
Now look, the wise men, the magi, and the [?] came before me to read this writing and show me its interpretation, but they could not explain it to me.

I have heard about you that you can explain interpretations. Now, if you can read the writing and show me its interpretation, you will be clothed in purple, with a gold chain around your neck, and you will rule as third in my kingdom.”
Daniel said before the king, “Keep your gifts for yourself, and give the honor of your house to someone else. But I will read the writing and show you its interpretation.
O king, the Most High God gave greatness, kingship, honor, and glory to your father Nebuchadnezzar.

Because of the greatness he gave him, all nations, peoples, and languages were terrified and trembled before him. He struck whomever he wished, killed whomever he wished, raised up whomever he wished, and brought low whomever he wished.
But when his heart became exalted and his spirit grew strong in arrogance, he fell from his royal throne, and his honor was taken away from him.

He was driven away from human beings, and he was given a heart like that of wild beasts. He lived with the wild donkeys, and they fed him grass like an ox. His body was drenched with the dew of heaven until he recognized that the Most High God rules over the kingdom of human beings and gives it to whomever he wishes.
But you, his son Belshazzar, did not humble your heart before God, although you knew all this.

You became arrogant against the God of heaven, and the vessels of his house were brought before you. You and your nobles, your concubines, and your wives drank wine from them. You praised the gods of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which neither see nor hear nor understand. But you did not glorify the God in whose hand are your breath and all your ways.
For this reason, the hand was sent from his presence and wrote this writing.
This is the writing that was written: Mene, Tekel, Peres.
This is the interpretation of the word: Mene—God has measured your kingdom and brought it to an end.
Tekel: it was weighed in the scales and found wanting.
Peres—your kingdom has been divided and given to the Medes and Persians.”
Then Belshazzar gave an order, and they clothed Daniel in purple and put a gold chain around his neck. A herald proclaimed before him that he was to be the third ruler in the kingdom.
That same night Belshazzar, king of the Chaldeans, was killed.
King Darius received the kingdom when he was sixty-two years old.
Darius thought it good to appoint one hundred and twenty governors over the kingdom, to serve throughout his kingdom.
Over them he appointed three administrators, one of whom was Daniel, to give orders to those governors so that the king would have no trouble.
Daniel surpassed them because an exceptional spirit was in him, and the king appointed him over his entire kingdom.

The administrators and governors were jealous and sought grounds for an accusation against Daniel. But they found no grounds, wrongdoing, or cause for complaint against him at all, because he was faithful.
The administrators said, “We cannot find any grounds for an accusation against Daniel except in the law of his God.”
Then the administrators and governors stood before the king and said to him, “King Darius, live forever!”

All the military commanders, nobles, princes, and governors in your kingdom have agreed to establish a royal decree and enforce an ordinance that anyone who makes a request of any god or human being for thirty days, except of you, O king, shall be thrown into the lions’ den.
Now, O king, establish the ordinance and put it in writing, so that it cannot be altered, according to the law of the Medes and Persians.
Then King Darius ordered the decree to be written.

When Daniel learned that the decree had been established, he went into his house. The windows of his upper room were open toward Jerusalem, and three times a day he knelt, prayed, and gave thanks before his God, just as he had done before.
Then those men watched and found Daniel praying and pleading with his God.

They approached the king and said, “O king, did you not establish an ordinance that anyone who makes a request of any god or human being for thirty days, except of you, O king, shall be thrown into the lions’ den?” The king said, “What you say is true, and it is not lawful to change the decree of the Medes and Persians.”
Then they answered the king and said, “Daniel, who is one of the captives from Judea, has not obeyed your decree, O king, and makes requests of his God three times.”
When the king heard this, he was deeply distressed. He sought to rescue Daniel and worked until midday to save him.
Then those men said to the king, “Know, O king, that it is not lawful to change the decree of the Medes and Persians, or any ordinance or enactment that the king establishes.”
Then the king gave the command, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the lions’ den. The king said to Daniel, “May the God whom you continually serve rescue you.”
They brought a stone and placed it over the den, and the king sealed it with his own signet ring and the signet rings of his nobles, so that nothing concerning Daniel could be changed in any way.
And the king went to his house and lay down without supper, and no delicacies were brought before him, and sleep deserted him. And God shut the mouths of the lions, and they did not harm Daniel.
Then the king rose at the first light of morning and hurried to the lions’ den.

When he approached the den, he cried out in a loud voice and said, “Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you continually served, been able to rescue you from the mouths of those lions?”
Daniel said to the king, “O king, live forever!
My God sent his angel and shut the mouths of these lions, and they did not harm me, because I was found innocent before him. Nor have I done any harm before you, O king.”

Then the king rejoiced within himself and ordered Daniel to be brought up out of the den. Daniel was brought up out of the den, and no injury at all was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.

And the king gave an order, and they brought the men who had slandered Daniel and threw them into the lions’ den, along with their children and their wives. They had not yet reached the bottom of the den when the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.
Then King Darius wrote to all the nations, peoples, and languages dwelling throughout the earth: “May peace abound for you.

I have issued this decree throughout the entire dominion of my kingdom: people are to fear and tremble before the God of Daniel, for he is the living God and endures forever. His kingdom will not be destroyed, and his dominion lasts to the end.
He helps and rescues, and performs signs in heaven and on earth. He rescued Daniel from the mouths of the lions.”
Daniel prospered during the reigns of Darius and Cyrus the Persian.
In the first year of Belshazzar, king of the Chaldeans, Daniel saw a dream and a vision in his mind while on his bed, and he wrote down the dream.
I, Daniel, was watching in the night vision, and behold, the four winds of heaven were beating against the great sea.
Four great beasts were coming up out of the sea, each different from the others.

The first was like a winged lioness, and its wings were like an eagle’s. I watched until its wings were plucked off, and it was removed from the earth and stood upright on human feet, and a human heart was given to it.
And behold, the second beast was like a bear, and it stood on one side. It had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth, and they said to it, “Arise, eat the flesh of many.”
After this I watched, and behold, another beast was like a leopard, with four bird’s wings on its back. The beast had four heads, and authority was given to it.

After this I watched, and behold, the fourth beast was terrifying, astonishing, and exceedingly powerful. Its teeth were iron. It devoured and crushed, and trampled what remained underfoot. It was very different from all the beasts before it, and it had ten horns.

I gazed in amazement at its horns, and behold, another small horn was coming up among them, and three of the earlier horns were uprooted before it. And behold, this horn had eyes like human eyes and a mouth that spoke great things.

I watched until thrones were cast down and the Ancient of Days sat down. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head was like pure wool. His throne was like a flame of fire, and its wheels were like blazing fire.
A river of fire poured out from before him. Thousands upon thousands served him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. The court sat, and the books were opened.
Then I watched because of the sound of the great words that the horn was speaking, until the beast was taken away and destroyed, and its body was given over to be burned with fire.
The authority of the other beasts was taken away, but their lives were prolonged for a time and times.
I watched in the vision of the night, and behold, one like a son of man was coming with the clouds of heaven. He reached the Ancient of Days and was brought before him.

Authority, honor, and a kingdom were given to him, and all nations, peoples, and languages shall serve him. His authority is an everlasting authority that does not pass away, and his kingdom shall not be destroyed.
My flesh trembled within me—I, Daniel—and the vision in my head troubled me.
I approached one of those standing there and sought to learn the truth about all this. He told me the truth and showed me the interpretation of these things.
“These great beasts are four kingdoms that will arise on the earth and be removed.
And the holy ones of the Most High shall receive the kingdom and hold it forever and ever.”

Then I sought to know the truth about the fourth beast, because it was very different from all the other beasts and exceedingly terrifying. Its teeth were iron and its claws bronze. It devoured and crushed, and trampled what remained underfoot.

I also sought to know about the ten horns on its head and about the other horn that came up and cast out three of them, which had eyes and a mouth that spoke great things, and whose appearance was greater than that of the others.
I watched, and that horn waged war against the holy ones and prevailed over them,
until the Ancient of Days came and gave justice to the holy ones of the Most High. The time arrived, and the holy ones took possession of the kingdom.
And he said, “The fourth beast shall be a fourth kingdom on earth, which shall be greater than all the kingdoms. It shall devour the whole earth, trample it, and crush it.
Its ten horns are ten kings who shall arise, and after them another shall arise who shall surpass all the earlier ones in wickedness, and he shall bring three kings low.

He will speak words against the Most High and lead the holy ones of the Most High astray. He will intend to change the times and the laws, and they will be handed over to him for a time, times, and half a time.
The court will sit, and they will take away his dominion, to destroy and annihilate it completely.
The kingdom, dominion, and greatness of the kings under all heaven were given to the holy ones of the Most High. His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions will serve and obey him.
Here the account ends. My thoughts greatly troubled me, Daniel, and the color of my face changed, and I kept the matter in my heart.
In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar, a vision appeared to me.
I, Daniel, after the first vision, was in Susa, in the citadel that is in the land of Elam, and I was beside the Ulai.
I lifted my eyes and saw, and there was a ram standing opposite the Ulai. Its horns were high, and one was higher than the other, and the higher one came up afterward.
I saw the ram charging toward the sea, toward the north, and toward the south. No beasts could stand before it, and none could escape its power. It did as it pleased and grew great.
As I watched, a male goat came from the west across the surface of the earth without touching the ground. The goat had one horn between its eyes.
And it came up to the horned ram that I had seen standing opposite the Ulai, and charged at it with all its strength.

I saw it come up to the ram. It became enraged, struck the ram, and broke both its horns. The ram had no strength to withstand it. It threw the ram to the ground and trampled it under its feet, and there was no one to rescue the ram from the goat's power.
The male goat grew exceedingly great, but when it became strong, its great horn was broken. Four other horns came up in its place toward the four winds of heaven.
From one of them came a mighty horn, and it grew still greater toward the north.
It gained strength and rose as high as the hosts of heaven. It cast some of the heavenly host and some of the stars down to the earth and trampled them.
Until the commander frees the captives, and through him the sacrifices were disrupted, and it came to pass, and he prospered, and the sanctuary will be laid waste.
Sins were laid upon the sacrifices, and righteousness fell to the ground. It acted and prospered.

I heard one of the holy ones speaking, and a holy one said to Phelmon, who was speaking, "How long will this vision last, with the sacrifices taken away, the sins of desolation imposed, and the sanctuary and the host trampled?"
He said to him, "Until evening and morning, two thousand three hundred days, and the sanctuary will be cleansed."
When I, Daniel, saw the vision and sought to understand it, someone with the appearance of a man stood before me.
I heard a man's voice from the midst of the Ulai. It called out and said, "Gabriel, make him understand this vision."
He came and stood where I was standing. At his approach I became dazed and fell on my face. He said to me, "Understand, son of man, that the vision concerns the time of the end."
While he was speaking with me, I became dazed and fell face down on the ground. He took hold of me and set me on my feet.
He said to me, "Look, I will show you what will happen upon the earth at the end, for the end is still at the appointed time."
The horned ram that you saw is the king of the Persians and the Medes.
The male goat is the king of the Greeks, and the great horn between its eyes is the first king.
As for its being broken and the other horns taking its place, four kings will arise from its nation, but not by their own power.
After their reign, when their sins have reached their fullness, a king with a brazen face, skilled in riddles, will arise.
His power will be mighty, and he will destroy wondrous things. He will prosper and act, and he will destroy the mighty and the holy people.

And his [?] yoke will prosper, and deceit will prosper in his hands. He will become arrogant in his heart, and through deceit he will destroy many. He will stand for the destruction of many and crush them like eggs in his hand.
The vision of the evening and the morning that was spoken is true. But you must seal the vision, for it concerns many days to come.
And I, Daniel, slept and became ill. Then I rose and carried out the king’s business. I was astonished at the vision, and there was no one who could explain it.
In the first year of Darius, son of Ahasuerus, of Median descent, who reigned over the kingdom of the Chaldeans,
I, Daniel, understood from the books the number of years concerning which the word of the Lord had come to Jeremiah the prophet: seventy years until the desolation of Jerusalem was completed.
And I turned my face toward the Lord my God to seek him with prayers and supplications, with fasting and sackcloth.
I prayed to the Lord God, gave thanks, and said, “Lord, great and wonderful God, who keeps the covenant and shows mercy to those who love you and keep your commandments,
We have sinned, acted lawlessly, done wrong, rebelled, and turned away from your commandments and your ordinances.
we did not listen to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our rulers, our fathers, and all the people of the land.

Righteousness belongs to you, Lord, but shame belongs to us, as it does this day—to the men of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and all Israel, both near and far, in every land where you scattered them because of the disobedience with which they disobeyed you.
Lord, shame belongs to our faces, to our kings, to our rulers, and to our fathers, for we have sinned.
And compassion and forgiveness belong to the Lord our God, for we rebelled against the Lord.
We did not listen to the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in his laws, which he set before us through his servants the prophets.

All Israel transgressed your laws and turned aside so as not to listen to your voice. And the curses and the oath written in the law of Moses, your servant, Lord, came upon us, because we sinned against him.

He confirmed the words that he had spoken against us and against our judges who judged us, bringing great calamities upon us. Under the whole heaven, nothing like what happened in Jerusalem had happened.

As it is written in the law of Moses, all these calamities came upon us. Yet we did not seek the favor of the Lord our God by turning from the iniquities of our fathers and coming to understand all your truth.
And the Lord our God kept watch over our calamities and brought them upon us, for the Lord our God is righteous in all the deeds he has done to us, because we did not obey his voice.
And now, Lord our God, who brought your people out of the land of the Egyptians with a mighty hand and made a name for yourself, as it remains this day: we have sinned and acted lawlessly.

Lord, in all your mercy, let your wrath turn away and your anger be lifted from your city Jerusalem, your holy mountain, for we have sinned, and because of our lawlessness and that of our fathers, Jerusalem and all your people have become a reproach to everyone around us.
And now, Lord our God, hear the prayers and petitions of your servant, and for your own sake show your face upon the sanctuary that has been laid waste.

Incline your ear, my God, and hear me. Open your eyes and see our devastation and that of your city, over which your name is called. For we lay our supplications before you not because of our righteousness, but because of your great compassion.
Lord, hear! Lord, forgive! Lord, listen! Lord, do not delay, for your own sake, my God, because your name is called over your city.”
While I was speaking and praying, confessing my sins and the sins of the people of Israel, and laying my supplications before the Lord my God concerning the holy mountain,
while I was still speaking in prayer, behold, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the first vision, came flying and approached me about the time of the evening sacrifice.
He gave me understanding, spoke with me, and said, “Daniel, I have now come to give you understanding.
At the beginning of your prayers a message went out, and I have come to tell you, for you are a dearly loved man. Now consider the message and understand the vision.

Seventy weeks have been decreed for your people and for the holy city, to bring sins to an end, to seal up lawless deeds, to wipe away injustices, to atone for ungodliness, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal the vision and the prophet, and to anoint the Holy of Holies.

Know and understand: from the going forth of the word to give an answer and to rebuild Jerusalem until the Anointed One, the ruler, there will be seven weeks and sixty-two weeks. The squares and walls will be restored and rebuilt, and the times will be renewed.

After the sixty-two weeks, the anointing will be removed, and there will be no justice in it. The city and the sanctuary will be destroyed along with the ruler who is to come, and they will be swept away by a flood. Until the end of the shortened war, he will decree destruction. He will strengthen a covenant with many for one week, and for half a week he will put an end to the altars and sacrifices. At the extremities of the corner there will be destruction, and until the end and the distress he will decree what is to come upon the destruction.

He will strengthen a covenant with many for one week, and for half a week sacrifices and offerings will be removed. The abomination of desolation will stand upon the temple, and until the end of the appointed time, the final judgment will be poured out upon the desolation.
The sixth vision

In the third year of Cyrus, king of Persia, a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar. The word was true, and the power was great, and understanding was given to him in the vision.
In those days I, Daniel, was mourning for three weeks.
I ate no desirable bread, and neither meat nor wine entered my mouth. I did not anoint myself with oil until the three weeks were completed.
On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was standing on the bank of the great river, which is the Tigris, the Diglath.
I raised my eyes, and there was a man clothed in splendor, with a belt of gold from Uphaz around his waist.

His body was the color of the sea, his face was like the appearance of lightning, and his eyes were like rays of fire. His arms and thighs were like the appearance of gleaming bronze, and the sound of his words was like the sound of an army.
I, Daniel, alone saw the vision. The men who were with me did not see the vision, but great fear fell upon them, and they fled in terror.
I was left alone and saw that great vision. No strength remained in me, my splendor turned to ruin, and I could not remain strong.
I heard the sound of his words, and as I heard the sound of his words, I stood stunned, with my face bowed to the ground.
Then a hand stretched out toward me and raised me onto my knees and the palms of my hands.

He said to me, “Daniel, greatly beloved man, understand the words that I will speak to you, and stand in your place, for I have now been sent to you.” As he spoke these words to me, I stood up trembling.
He said to me, “Do not be afraid, Daniel, for from the day you set your heart to understand and to afflict yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come because of your words.
The prince of the kingdom of Persia opposed me for twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, and I left him there with the prince of the kingdom of Persia.
I have come to make you understand what events will befall your people in the last days, for the vision concerns days yet to come.”
As he spoke these words to me, I fell facedown to the ground and remained stunned.

And behold, one resembling a son of man approached my lips. I opened my mouth and spoke, saying to the man standing before me, “Lord, when you appeared to me, my inward parts were troubled within me, and there is no strength in me.”
“How can your servant, lord, speak with my lord? I no longer have strength to stand, and no breath remains in me.”
Again, one who looked like a man approached me and strengthened me.
He said, “Do not be afraid, greatly beloved man. Peace be with you. Be strong and courageous.” As he spoke with me, I became strong and said, “Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me.”
He said, “Do you know why I have come to you? Now I will return to wage war against the prince of Persia. As I was going, the prince of Greece was coming.”
“But I will tell you what is set down in the book of truth. No one helps me in these matters except Michael, your prince.”
“In the first year of Cyrus, I stood to provide support and strength.”

“Now I will tell you the truth. Behold, three kings will arise in the land of Persia, and the fourth will become far wealthier than all of them. After becoming strong through his wealth, he will rise against the kingdoms of Greece.”
“A mighty king will arise, rule over a great dominion, and do as he pleases.”

“When he arises, his kingdom will be shattered and divided toward the four winds of heaven, but not for his posterity, nor according to the dominion with which he ruled. For his kingdom will be uprooted and belong to others besides them.”
And the king of the south will become strong, and one of the princes will become stronger than he and will exercise great dominion.

“After their years, they will join with one another. The daughter of the king of the south will come to the king of the north to make treaties with him. But she will not retain the strength of her arm, and his offspring will not stand. She herself will be handed over, along with those who brought her, the maiden, and the one who strengthened her at that time.”
“A shoot from her root will arise in his appointed position. He will come against the army and enter the strongholds of the northern kingdom. He will act against them and become strong.”

“He will overthrow their gods along with their cast images, and he will carry all their precious vessels of gold and silver away as plunder to Egypt. He himself will become more firmly established than the king of the north.”
“He will enter the kingdom of the king of the south and return to his own land.”
“His sons will gather a multitude of many troops. He will advance and enter, flood through and pass on, then stop and be stirred up as far as his stronghold.”
“The king of the south will become enraged, go out, and wage war against the king of the north. He will assemble a large army, and the army will be delivered into his hands.”
“He will take away the multitude, and his heart will become proud. He will overthrow tens of thousands, but he will not become strong.”
“The king of the north will return and bring an army larger than the first. At the end of the appointed times, he will come and enter with a great army and abundant possessions.”
“At those times, many will rise against the king of the south. The sons of the survivors of your people will rise up to fulfill the vision, but they will become weak.”
And the king of the south will come and heap up earth and capture fortified cities. The king’s forces will not stand firm, and his chosen men will rise up, but there will be no strength to stand.
“When he comes against him, he will do as he pleases, and no one will be able to withstand him. He will stand in the land of Sabim, and it will meet its end at his hands.”

“He will set his face to enter all his kingdoms with his strength, and he will make entirely fair agreements with him. He will give him the daughter of women for destruction. Let her not become strong, and let her not belong to him.”
“He will turn his face toward the islands and capture many of them. He will burn the rulers who insulted them, and he will turn their insults back upon their own faces.”
He will return to his own land with force, but he will grow weak and fall and will not be found.
A shoot of kingship will arise from his root in his place, and he will forcibly bring about the splendor of the kingdom. In those days he will be crushed, neither face to face nor through war.
He will stand in his own place, because he was despised and they did not give him royal glory. He will come successfully and seize kingdoms through enticements.
The forces that surge like a flood will be swept away before him, and the leader of the covenant will be crushed.
He will deal deceitfully with those who join him, and he will rise and become powerful over them with a small nation.

He will come successfully through many lands and do what neither his fathers nor his fathers’ fathers did. He will distribute plunder, spoil, and possessions among them, and he will devise plans against the Egyptians for a time.

He will stir up his strength and his heart against the king of the south with a great force. The king of the south will prepare for battle with a great and very powerful army, but he will not remain firm, because they will devise plans against him.
They will eat whatever is allotted to him and will crush him. They will burn the army, and many wounded will fall.
And the hearts of both kings will be intent on evil, and they will speak lies at the same table, but it will not succeed, for the end is at the appointed times.
He will return to his own land with great wealth, and his heart will be against the holy covenant. He will act and return to his own land.
At the appointed time he will return and come against the south, but the last occasion will not be like the first.

The armies of the Kittim will come against him, and he will be humbled and turn back. He will become angry against the holy covenant and act. He will return and join with those who abandoned the holy covenant.
Descendants will arise from him and violently defile the sanctuary. They will remove the continual offering and establish an abomination of destruction.
Those who corrupt the covenant will bring a stumbling block upon themselves, but the people who know their God will become strong and act.
Those among the people who have understanding will comprehend many things, but they will grow weak through sword, fire, captivity, and plunder for a number of days.
When they grow weak, they will find a little help, and many will join them through enticements.
Some of those who have understanding will grow weak, to test them, sift them, and reveal them until the end of the appointed time, because there is still time.

The king will act according to his own will. He will exalt himself and become proud above all gods, and he will speak arrogant things against the God of gods. He will prosper until the wrath comes to an end, for it is destined to come to an end.
He will give thought to the gods of his fathers and to the desire of women, but he will give no thought to any gods, and he will exalt himself above everything.
He will glorify the mighty God from his own place, and he will glorify a god whom his fathers did not know with gold, silver, precious stones, and desirable things.
He will pass into the days of fugitives in accordance with a foreign god. He will increase glory, subject many to him, and divide the land as a reward.

At the time of the end he will contend with the king of the south, and the king of the north will muster forces against him with chariots, horsemen, and many ships. He will enter the land, crush it, and pass through.
He will enter the land of Sabaim, and many will grow weak. These will escape from his hands: Edom, Moab, and the dominion of the children of Ammon.
And he will stretch out his hand over the land, and the land of the Egyptians will not be delivered.
He will rule over the hidden stores of gold and silver and over all the desirable possessions of the Egyptians, Libyans, and Ethiopians in their strongholds.
Then reports and alarms from the east and the north will spur him on, and he will come in great anger to destroy many.
And he will pitch his tent at Ephagnon, between the seas, on the holy mountain of Sabain. He will come as far as one side of it, and there will be no one to rescue him.

And at that time Michael, the great prince who stands over the children of your people, will arise. There will be a time of distress, such distress as has never occurred since a nation first existed on earth until that time. And at that time your people will be delivered, everyone who is found written in the book.
And many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will arise, some to everlasting life and some to reproach and everlasting shame.
And the wise will shine like the brightness of the firmament, and many of the righteous like the stars forever and ever.
And you, Daniel, shut up these words and seal the book until the time of the end, until many learn and knowledge increases.
And I, Daniel, looked, and behold, two were standing, on this side and on that side of the river.
And they said to the man who was dressed in linen and stood above the waters of the river, “How long will it be until the end of these wonders that you have spoken of?”

And I heard the man who was dressed in linen and stood above the waters of the river. He raised his right hand and his left hand to heaven and swore by the one who lives forever that it would be for a time, times, and half a time, and that when the scattering of the power of the holy people is complete, they will know all these things.
And I heard but did not understand, and I said, “Lord, what is the outcome of these things?”
And he said, “Go, Daniel, for these words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end.”
Many will be chosen, made white, tested, and purified, and the lawless will act lawlessly. The ungodly will not understand, but the wise will understand.
From the time of the changing of the continual offering and the setting up of the abomination of desolation, there will be one thousand two hundred thirty-five days.
And blessed is the one who endures and reaches one thousand three hundred and thirty-five days.
And you, come and rest, for there are still days and times until the completion of the end. And you will rest and arise at your time, at the end of the days.
